params.prompt:
1950s theatrical cartoon slapstick, hand-drawn colored-pencil pencil-test animation on cream paper, held on twos with visible line boil. Fixed camera, locked tripod, one continuous shot.

The round grey cartoon creature with the big pointed ears and the wide friendly grin coils its whole body back, throwing arm cocked behind its ear and tail up, and whips a small dart at the dartboard in a hard smear. The dart buries itself in the plaster a foot wide of the board. It throws both arms overhead in triumph anyway and hops on the spot, delighted. It sweeps another dart off the round side table, coils back even harder, and whips that one at the wall too.

Its face is exactly two red-orange eyes and one wide grin of small teeth, the same two eyes and the same grin in every frame. Its two tall pointed ears are the same two ears in every frame. Its feet come back down to the floor after every hop. It stays small, no taller than a third of the tall bookshelf of binders at frame right, in every frame.

Squash and stretch on every accent, smear frames through the fast arcs, snappy timing, elastic overshoot, comic energy.
